simple.meaning: עֲמָלֵקִי (ʻĂmâlêqîy) appears 12 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a son in the family line and in connection with flocks.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Genesis, Numbers, Judges, 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, beginning at Genesis 14:7. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family line, sacrifice, death, land, mountain, wilderness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עֲמָלֵקִי (H6003) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows עֲמָלֵקִי through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: עֲמָלֵקִי (ʻĂmâlêqîy) / H6003 is tracked through Genesis 14:7, Numbers 14:25, Numbers 14:43, Numbers 14:45. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

timeline.evidenceText: They returned, and came to En Mishpat (also called Kadesh), and struck all the country of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites, that lived in Hazazon Tamar.
Since the Amalekite and the Canaanite dwell in the valley, tomorrow turn and go into the wilderness by the way to the Red Sea.”
For there the Amalekite and the Canaanite are before you, and you will fall by the sword because you turned back from following Yahweh; therefore Yahweh will not be with you.”
Then the Amalekites came down, and the Canaanites who lived in that mountain, and struck them and beat them down, even to Hormah.
Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite died, and was buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.

Saul said to the Kenites, “Go, depart, go down from among the Amalekites, lest I destroy you with them; for you showed kindness to all the children of Israel, when they came up out of Egypt.” So the Kenites departed from among the Amalekites.
Saul said, “They have brought them from the Amalekites; for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the cattle, to sacrifice to Yahweh your God. We have utterly destroyed the rest.”
David and his men went up and raided the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites; for those were the inhabitants of the land, who were of old, on the way to Shur, even to the land of Egypt.
When David and his men had come to Ziklag on the third day, the Amalekites had made a raid on the South, and on Ziklag, and had struck Ziklag, and burned it with fire,
David asked him, “To whom do you belong? Where are you from?”
He said to me, ‘Who are you?’ I answered him, ‘I am an Amalekite.’
David said to the young man who told him, “Where are you from?”

definitions.full: H6003. Amaleqi עֲמָלֵקִי adjective, of a people 1Sam 30:13 ; 2Sam 1:13 , also (as predicate) 1:8 ; collective = ( the ) Amalekites 1Sam 15:6 , 15 ; 30:1 , elsewhere with article ׳הָע Num 14:25 , 43 , 45 (J; all + הַכְּנַעֲנִי ), 1Sam 27:8 ; הָע ׳שְׂדֵה Gen 14:7 ; הָע ׳הַר Judg 12:15 (in Ephraim); read ׳הָע also 1:16 (for הָעָם ) Bu GFM, > עֲמָלֵק Hollenb Mey Kit Kau ; on 2Sam 1:1 see foregoing. I. עָמַם verb (√ of following compare Arabic be comprehensive, include ; company ; also paternal uncle ; perhaps Assyrian ummanu, people; Sabean עם either ( a ) people , or ( b ) paternal uncle CIS iv. p. 20 ; plural suffix אעממהו = ( b ) Mordtm Himj. Inschr. 45. 70 ; also often in proper name CIS iv. No. 5, 1, 99, 7 etc. , Prät Neue Beitr. 25 Hom Chrest. 12, 133; A. und A. 6 We GGN 1893, 480 ).
